title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors, employees and contractors of Sims Limited and its related bodies corporate, globally. This tier is bound by the insider trading prohibition and the black-out periods, but not by the approval-to-deal process or the 'other types of restricted dealings' bans.

tiers.name: Restricted Employees
tiers.description: Employees notified by the Company Secretary that they are restricted because they are likely to possess inside information. Comprises Directors and Officers, Key Management Personnel, Executives, and employees formally notified because they regularly access sensitive information or are on a distribution, confidential project or insider list. All the substantive bans (secured financing, derivatives, short-term trading, short selling, hedging) and the prior approval requirement attach to this tier.

tiers.name: Directors and Officers
tiers.description: Directors and officers of Sims Limited, a listed sub-category of Restricted Employees. No separate rules or approver are specified for them.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons named in Sims' Remuneration Report, a listed sub-category of Restricted Employees. No separate rules or approver are specified for them.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Members of Sims' Executive Leadership Team, a listed sub-category of Restricted Employees. No separate rules or approver are specified for them.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: The Company Secretary, who administers approvals for everyone else and must direct their own requests to deal, including exceptional circumstances requests, to the Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Persons closely associated with Employees
tiers.description: Family members (spouse, civil partner, dependent children or stepchildren and relatives sharing the household for at least one year) and companies, trusts, partnerships or entities managed by, established for the benefit of, controlled directly or indirectly by, or whose economic interests are substantially equivalent to, the Employee or a family member. Subject to the same dealing restrictions as the Employee.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Sims Board may specify any other period as a black-out period from time to time. The policy does not state how such a period is communicated or whether the reason is confidential, though a refusal or revocation of approval must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: A flat ban on trading in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims' securities, with no venue limitation, so exchange-traded and OTC puts and calls are equally caught. No approval, waiver or exceptional circumstances route applies to this list of restricted dealings; the Company Secretary's approval power is directed at ordinary dealings and at black-out period sales.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees must not undertake any of the following dealings with respect to Sims’ securities: ... trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;

rules.section: Insider Trading Restrictions; Other types of restricted dealings
rules.detail: The derivatives ban is expressed to bind Restricted Employees only. For other Employees, a derivative over Sims' securities is a dealing in 'financial instruments linked to' Sims' securities, so it is barred during black-out periods and while holding inside information, but no prior approval is required.
rules.evidence: dealing (including on behalf of a third party) in Sims’ securities, including in any shares, options or rights to shares, bonds or other forms of securitised debt, notes, depositary receipts and any financial instruments linked to them.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims' securities. The policy draws no distinction between unvested plan securities, vested but restricted securities and freely held shares, so the ban covers all of them.
rules.evidence: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition sits in the 'Other types of restricted dealings' section, which applies only to Restricted Employees. Hedging by other Employees is not addressed, and remains subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the black-out periods.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collars are not named. Any such structure is a derivative product in respect of Sims' securities and a hedging arrangement limiting exposure to them, and if it is funded it is also a secured financing arrangement, so it fails three of the five restricted dealing bullets at once.
rules.evidence: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities; ... enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is prohibited outright for Restricted Employees, with no definition of the practice and no approval route. Not addressed for other Employees.
rules.evidence: engage in the practice of “short-selling” in Sims’ securities;

rules.section: Insider Trading Restrictions; Additional Dealing Restrictions on Restricted Employees
rules.detail: Securities lending is not named in the restricted dealings list. A stock loan is a transaction affecting title to, or an interest in, securities and involves transferring shares, so it is a dealing requiring the Company Secretary's prior written approval and is barred in black-out periods. Lending to facilitate a short position would also offend the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to, or an interest in securities, such as buying, selling or transferring shares, using Sims’ shares as security for a loan and entering into an agreement (or exercising an option) to buy or sell securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are not named, but a CFD is a derivative product issued in respect of Sims' securities and so falls within the derivatives ban; a short CFD would also breach the short selling prohibition.
rules.evidence: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;

rules.detail: Margin loans in respect of Sims' securities are prohibited for Restricted Employees, with no grandfathering language, no approval route and no guidance on gearing levels, price triggers, margin calls or forced sales.
rules.evidence: enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims’ securities;

rules.section: Other types of restricted dealings; Insider Trading Restrictions
rules.detail: Using Sims' shares as security for a loan is expressly a dealing, and granting that security is prohibited for Restricted Employees as a secured financing arrangement. A charge or lien unconnected with any financing is not separately addressed, but would still be a dealing affecting an interest in securities requiring approval.
rules.evidence: using Sims’ shares as security for a loan

rules.detail: For Employees who are not Restricted Employees, using Sims' shares as security for a loan is a dealing, so it may not occur during a black-out period or while holding inside information, but the secured financing ban and the prior approval process do not apply to them.
rules.evidence: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to, or an interest in securities, such as buying, selling or transferring shares, using Sims’ shares as security for a loan

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin loans: 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims' securities' captures a bespoke bank loan secured on the shares, whatever the lender or the loan to value ratio, and applies to vested and unvested holdings alike. There is no exemption authority for this bullet.
rules.evidence: enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims’ securities;

rules.detail: A three-month short-term trading ban with a single carve-out for the sale of securities received under an employee incentive scheme where approval has been obtained. The policy does not state whether the three months runs from acquisition or on a LIFO basis.
rules.evidence: deal in Sims’ securities on a short-term trading basis (being three months), other than the sale of securities received under an employee incentive scheme where approval to deal under this policy has been obtained;

clearance.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions on Restricted Employees; Conditions of Approval to Trade
clearance.evidence: Wait for written approval from the Company Secretary (or their delegate), who will provide a response in writing within two business days after the initial approval request. Upon receipt of approval, complete the dealing within two business days (commencing the day after approval is provided) otherwise approval must be sought again.

clearance.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions on Restricted Employees
clearance.evidence: If the Company Secretary is making a request to deal in Sims’ securities, it must do so to the Chief Executive Officer.

clearance.section: Additional Dealing Restrictions on Restricted Employees
clearance.evidence: Prior to any proposed dealing in Sims’ securities, Restricted Employees must first confirm that they are not in possession of any inside information and take the following steps

carve_outs: the sale of securities received under an employee incentive scheme where approval to deal under this policy has been obtained
short_term.evidence: deal in Sims’ securities on a short-term trading basis (being three months), other than the sale of securities received under an employee incentive scheme where approval to deal under this policy has been obtained;

exceptions.approver: Company Secretary (or their delegate); the Chief Executive Officer where the applicant is the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: Employees (including Restricted Employees) who need to sell (but not buy) Sims’ securities during a black-out period due to exceptional circumstances (including severe financial hardship (excluding tax liabilities) or compulsion by a court order), must first confirm that they are not in possession of any inside information

exceptions.approver: Company Secretary (or their delegate); the Chief Executive Officer where the applicant is the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: exceptional circumstances (including severe financial hardship (excluding tax liabilities) or compulsion by a court order)
acquisition of securities through a dividend reinvestment plan or share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders
acquisition of securities under a pro rata issue; disposal of rights acquired under a pro rata issue
disposal of securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

acquisition of securities under an employee incentive scheme; however, for clarity, any subsequent dealing of securities which cease to be held under the terms of a scheme remains subject to the provisions of this policy

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (e.g. transfer of securities already held in a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee or persons closely associated is a beneficiary)

external_documents: Sims' Remuneration Report, which identifies Key Management Personnel
Sims' employee incentive scheme rules, referred to but not reproduced
exemption_authority: The Company Secretary (or delegate) may approve a sale, but not a purchase, during a black-out period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship (excluding tax liabilities) or compulsion by a court order, where the sale is the only reasonable course of action available; the Chief Executive Officer decides such requests from the Company Secretary. Approval may be given or refused at discretion, is final and binding, and may be withdrawn if circumstances change. No provision permits any waiver of the 'other types of restricted dealings' prohibitions on secured financing, derivatives, hedging, short selling or short-term trading.
jurisdiction_overlays: Policy scope is global, applying to Directors, employees and contractors of Sims Limited and its related bodies corporate across all countries of operation
Sims' American Depositary Shares are quoted on the US over-the-counter market (USOTC: SMSMY), though the policy imposes no separate US overlay

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees must not ... enter into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims’ securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for every director, officer, KMP and executive, with no approval or hardship route.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives ban with no venue limit
bespoke_clauses.clause: trade in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims’ securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put and written call are derivative products in respect of Sims' securities, so the protective legs are prohibited regardless of whether they are exchange-traded or written OTC by a bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to Sims’ securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is not confined to unvested or plan securities, so even a collar over long-held, freely tradeable shares is caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to, or an interest in securities, such as buying, selling or transferring shares, using Sims’ shares as security for a loan and entering into an agreement (or exercising an option) to buy or sell securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting the bank security over the shares is itself a dealing, so it is caught by black-out periods and the approval process even before the secured financing ban is reached.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The exceptional circumstances mechanism permits an Employee 'who need[s] to sell (but not buy) Sims’ securities during a black-out period' to seek approval; nothing in the policy permits approval of a restricted dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even severe financial hardship gives access only to a sale during a black-out period, never to a collar or a secured loan, so there is no route to the structure at all.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restrictions follow the tier, not the person
bespoke_clauses.clause: there are certain Employees that will be notified by the Company Secretary that they are restricted employees ... Restricted Employees include: Directors and Officers ... Key Management Personnel ... Executives
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bans bite on exactly the population a bank would target for a funded collar, while ordinary employees, who face no such bans, are not a commercially relevant client group.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Persons closely associated with Employees (including Restricted Employees) are subject to the same dealing restrictions that apply to that Employee ... companies, trusts, partnerships or entities ... the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to the Employee or a family member.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The economic equivalence limb defeats any attempt to place the collar or the loan in a family trust, controlled company or other vehicle.

bespoke_clauses.clause: How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for a dealing that is not prohibited, the Company Secretary applies a reputational perception test, and a director hedging their exposure would rarely survive it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Upon receipt of approval, complete the dealing within two business days (commencing the day after approval is provided) otherwise approval must be sought again. ... Approval to deal can be withdrawn if circumstances change.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted dealing must be documented and executed inside two business days and approval can be withdrawn, which would be impractical for a negotiated derivative even if one were permitted.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Sims director, officer, KMP or executive. The 'Other types of restricted dealings' section prohibits Restricted Employees from entering margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Sims' securities, from trading in derivative products issued over or in respect of Sims' securities, and from entering any hedging arrangements that limit exposure to them, so every element of the structure is separately banned. The bans apply to all holdings without distinguishing vested from unvested shares, extend to persons closely associated including controlled trusts and entities whose economic interests are substantially equivalent, and carry no approval, waiver or grandfathering route. The Company Secretary's exceptional circumstances power reaches only a sale, not a purchase, during a black-out period, so it cannot authorise a collar or a secured loan. Only Employees who are not Restricted Employees escape these bans, and for them a derivative or a share-secured loan is merely a dealing subject to the black-out periods and the insider trading prohibition.
